en: The *Maṇibhadra Sūtra*, translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Tanwulan of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park. At that time...
Together with a great assembly of bhikṣus,
he preached the Maṇiratna Sūtra.
The Buddha asked Ānanda:
For what reason do the people of the world fail to attain peace and security?
For what reason do the myriad subjects of the world suffer from many illnesses and ailments?
The occurrence of maternal abdominal pain, heartache, headaches, dizziness, and inability to eat or drink—
all these are the deeds of Māra.
Now, the bhikṣus are greatly terrified in this manner.
He then stepped forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"From where does suffering come, and to where does it go?
The people are filled with great sorrow and find no joy."
The Buddha assembled the bhikṣus— Mahākāśyapa, Vairaṭṭa, Aniruddha, Revata, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Śāriputra, Ānanda, and Nandika—
and thereupon preached the Maṇiratna Sūtra.
The Buddha then enumerated the names of the Buddhas:
first, Vipaśyin Buddha; second, Śikhin Buddha;
third, Viśvabhū Buddha; fourth, Krakucchanda Buddha.
The fifth was Konāgamana Buddha, the sixth was Kāśyapa Buddha,
and the seventh was Śākyamuni Buddha.
Now, this sutra has issued from the mouths of all these Buddhas.
The first is Śikṣāra, the second is Gandhara,
the third is Gandhula, the fourth is Mekhala,
the fifth is Kancula, and the sixth is Mayūra.
The seventh is Āśvala; the eighth is Anusamāna;
the ninth is Anusūnu; the tenth is Aṇḍika.
Among all the people, great and small alike, there are those who have contracted illnesses.
Now the Buddha commands all the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
and upāsikās to recite this sūtra.
There are spirits within the country.
There are ghosts of the mountains, ghosts of the forests,
ghosts of the grassy thickets, ghosts of the burial mounds,
ghosts within the burial mounds, and ghosts upon the ground.
There are ghosts within the water and ghosts by the water's edge;
there are ghosts within the fire and ghosts by the fire's edge;
there are ghosts of the Big Dipper and ghosts in the midst of space.
There are ghosts of the marketplace, ghosts of the dead,
ghosts of the living, hungry ghosts,
ghosts outside the Way, and ghosts within the Way.
There are ghosts outside the hall and ghosts within the hall;
there are ghosts within the body and ghosts outside the body;
there are ghosts that feed on food and ghosts that haunt during sleep.
Now the Buddha said: "There are red-colored ghosts and black-colored ghosts;
there are long ghosts and short ghosts;
there are large ghosts and small ghosts."
There are ghosts that dwell within the living;
there are white ghosts, yellow ghosts, blue ghosts,
black ghosts, and ghosts that appear in dreams and upon waking.
There are ghosts that arise at dawn and ghosts that walk on foot;
there are ghosts that fly and ghosts that inquire after people's souls and spirits;
there are ghosts of the living and ghosts of the dead.
The Buddha said: "If there arises the sword or staff of anger and hatred, one should in all cases recite this Maṇiratna Sūtra;
then all the ghosts and spirits will be shattered."
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"If there are those who receive this sutra,
or if there are those who are ill or emaciated, they should recite this sutra."
If one suffers from headaches, dizziness, chills and fevers, or heart afflictions,
they should constantly read this Maṇiratna Sūtra;
then all ghosts and spirits shall have their heads split into seven pieces.
If there are local officials, bandits, water,
or fire [disasters], one should then recite this Maṇiratna Sūtra;
then the various ghosts and spirits will no longer be able to harass or harm people.
Now, this sutra has issued from the mouths of all Buddhas.
If there are ghosts within a land—
firstly named Shen-sha and secondly named Fu-qiu.
These two demons are fierce in their pursuit of people's vulnerabilities;
if one suffers from headaches, dizziness, chills, fever, or heart affliction,
one should immediately invoke the names of these two demons.
Thereupon, he shall recite the Maṇidhāraṇī Sūtra;
there are no ghosts or spirits among them who will not be shattered.
Whether they be blue ghosts, yellow ghosts, or black ghosts.
Tall ghosts and short ghosts, large ghosts and small ghosts—
every kind of spirit and ghost, great and small,
who delights in harassing the people of the world.
Their ghosts are named the Kim-man ghosts and the Vaitaraṇī ghosts;
they are hungry ghosts, stingy and greedy ghosts,
ghosts of toil and suffering, and emaciated ghosts of disease.
There are ghosts of pain and itch, ghosts of thought and reflection;
ghosts within the body and ghosts outside the body;
ghosts with deformed limbs and ghosts who are lame or crippled.
The *vedanā-graha*, the *unmāda-graha*, the *mūḍha-graha*,
and the *badhira-graha*; the *mūka-graha*, the *śvasana-graha*,
the *rodana-graha*, and the *vyādhi-graha*.
The ghosts of depletion and exhaustion, the ghosts of jealousy,
the ghosts of *wangliang* and *yinghuo*,
the ghosts of wandering light, and the ghosts of suppression and cursing.
Curses, ghosts that lie in wait for the corpse, and ghosts that inject poison;
ghosts of leprosy and death, ghosts that dwell in government offices;
ghosts of military camps and ghosts that transmit illness through watchtowers.

The ghosts of those who died in prison; the ghosts of those who died as captives; the ghosts of those who died by water; the ghosts of those who drowned. The ghosts of those who died by fire; the ghosts of those who were burned to death.
The ghosts of those who died abroad and have not yet been buried; the ghosts of those who died in the marketplace.
The ghosts who die on the road, the ghosts who die of thirst,
the ghosts who die of hunger, the ghosts who die by drinking [poison],
the ghosts who die of cold, and the ghosts who die by the sword.
The blood-dying ghost, the stench-dying ghost;
the ghost of deferred prayer, the fighting ghost;
the club-killed ghost, the strangulation-killed ghost.
The ghost who hangs itself to death; the ghost who kills itself by stabbing;
the ghost of an enemy; the ghost of violent death;
the ghost of putrid skin; and the ghost that severs people's hair and body hair.
Blood-drinking ghosts, flying ghosts,
ghost-rider ghosts, chariot-driving ghosts,
walking ghosts, and encounter-averting ghosts.
Mountain spirits and stone spirits;
earth spirits and sea-shore spirits;
spirits of the ocean and spirits of bridges.
Ghosts within ditches and channels; ghosts on the roads;
ghosts outside the roads; ghosts of Hu and Yi peoples;
ghosts of Qiang and Lu barbarians; and ghosts that are the numinous sprites of trees.
The spirits of hundreds of insects; the spirits of birds and beasts;
the ghosts within mountain ravines and valley passes;
the ghosts at the gates of villages; and the ghosts within the household doors.
The ghosts of outdoor hearths and kitchen stoves;
the ghosts of filthy ponds and latrine deities;
the ghosts of sorcery and the ghosts of bewitching arts.
Neither spirits nor those who falsely claim to be spirits shall have dominion over them;
no ghosts or spirits, whether great or small,
shall be able to afflict or harm their bodies.
If any spirit or ghost does not follow my words,
their head shall split into seven pieces.
If there is a person who has fallen ill or become emaciated, [they shall be restored].
When these names of the various spirits above are recited,
those who are ill or emaciated shall immediately be cured.
This sutra has issued from the mouth of Śākyamuni Buddha.
When all the ghosts and spirits heard this sutra,
from this day forward they were all cured and healed. After the Buddha had finished preaching the sutra, [the assembly rejoiced].
The bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, and non-humans, all having received the Buddha’s grace, came forward, paid homage to the Buddha, and departed.
The Sūtra on Maṇibhadra Spoken by the Buddha
